title: SilverCove Q2 Inference Economics & Resilience Roadmap
next_steps: Redwood to send tailored pricing sheet and two reservation options by 2026-06-12
Schedule 1-hr perf benchmark with SilverCove engineers (model+seq len) week of 6/15
Share SOC 2 and KMS integration docs to Simone by 2026-06-11
action_items: Maya Chen: Prepare pricing + commitment scenarios (due 2026-06-12)
Diego Ramos: Draft benchmark plan and test cases for cart personalization model (due 2026-06-16)
Tom Alvarez: Provide representative prompt set, 95th perc latency target, and daily qps profile (due 2026-06-11)
Simone Li: Confirm procurement timeline and approval matrix (due 2026-06-18)
summary: Quarterly health and economics sync focused on cost drivers for high-volume personalization, tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated, resilience/failover strategy for holiday peak, and runway for a pilot commit. Action items include pricing scenarios, benchmark plan, and security docs exchange.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we got most people — Rachel, Tom, Simone?
[00:06] Rachel Park: Yep hi Maya, hi Diego, thanks — appreciate the time.
[00:10] Maya Chen: Cool, quick agenda: cost & usage review, propose commitment options, resilience plan for Q4, and then next steps.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: I'll jump into the perf parts after the econ bit.
[00:22] Tom Alvarez: Quick note — we've got a maintenance window 6/12 so if you schedule anything around then heads up.
[00:28] Maya Chen: Got it. Alright Rachel, do you want to start with a 60-second reminder of current usage?
[00:33] Rachel Park: Sure — so average daily calls to the personalization endpoint are about 4.2M tokens, peaks hit about 12M on promo days. Sequence length average is 220 tokens; p95 is 420. Rate profile is very spiky between 12:00 and 14:00 ET and during late evening conversions. We are seeing token growth ~18% month over month.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Nice detail. That growth is why we flagged the cost delta in May. Diego, do you have the cost breakdown slide?
[00:58] Diego Ramos: Yeah — so main drivers are: model choice (our vanilla 17B raft vs quantized 13B variant), KV cache hit rate, and lack of persistent batching. On hosted current effective cost is about $0.0085 per 1k in our numbers given your profile, but with improved batching and KV we can push that down to around $0.0055.
[01:20] Tom Alvarez: Wait 0.0055 — is that after you account for p95 latency constraints? Because we can't sacrifice the sub-200ms tail on add-to-cart flows.
[01:29] Diego Ramos: Good call — the 0.0055 case assumes canary-enabled KV caching and mild batching with strict per-request limits; p95 we modeled at 210ms. If you need sub-200ms consistently we'd be closer to 0.0068.
[01:42] Rachel Park: So it's a latency vs cost knob. Simone, from finance where are you on incremental spend?
[01:47] Simone Li: We're open to commitment if it buys predictability. My question is: what does dedicated get us besides a cheaper per-token? We need SLAs and predictable tail latency.
[01:56] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — you control pool size, consistent scheduling, and higher KV cache locality. Also we can provide SLA-backed latency targets and prioritized routing.
[02:07] Benji Reid: One more — what about cross-region failover? We can't have a single region outage take us down during prime.
[02:13] Diego Ramos: We recommend multi-region pairing with asynchronous warm pools. For peak events we can burst to hosted spare capacity in another region. There's a small additional egress/cross-region cost.
[02:24] Rachel Park: Do you have numbers on the additional cost for cross-region burst?
[02:27] Diego Ramos: Rough ballpark: add 8–12% to committed spend for standby warm pools; actual depends on ratio of standby to active.
[02:35] Simone Li: That sounds reasonable if SLAs and auditability are covered — we need audit logs for all inference calls for compliance.
[02:43] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide immutable audit logs and route them to your S3 or SIEM; Diego will follow up with the retention and encryption options.
[02:51] Diego Ramos: On encryption, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations in Private/Dedicated; hosted also supports KMS but with Redwood-managed key options.
[02:59] Tom Alvarez: We're leaning towards Dedicated for availability. The other question is around model quantization — will that impact accuracy in the personalization model?
[03:07] Diego Ramos: Potentially. We'll do a QA regression sweep across your prompt set; for some architectures 8-bit quantization is fine, for others we recommend mixed precision or q4_0/ q4_kh variants. The benchmark will tell us more.
[03:19] Rachel Park: Can we also run a rollout test where we shadow traffic to a quantized variant for two weeks?
[03:23] Maya Chen: Absolutely — that's a common canary pattern. We can talk about traffic split and guardrails in the pilot plan.
[03:29] Tom Alvarez: About the pilot — timeline we discussed internally is to have a pilot in July and then decide commit by mid-August. Is that feasible?
[03:36] Maya Chen: Yes, July pilot — we can scope a two-week performance and quality run with your datasets. Diego, I'll let you outline the technical plan.
[03:42] Diego Ramos: Plan: 1) collect representative prompt set and baseline outputs; 2) run perf tests at your peak qps and p95 seq; 3) run accuracy/regression checks comparing 17B vs quantized 13B; 4) evaluate cache hit improvements. We'll schedule a 90-min kick-off for the benchmark.
[03:59] Benji Reid: On observability, we need per-request token breakdown, latency histograms, and trace IDs forwarded into our jaeger.
[04:08] Diego Ramos: We can forward traces and export detailed token-level breakdowns. Note: token breakdowns in hosted mode are aggregated but we can provide per-request with Dedicated.
[04:20] Rachel Park: That aggregation has bitten us before — we need raw per-request token logs for model drift analysis.
[04:26] Maya Chen: Ok action: Diego to confirm what per-request telemetry looks like in dedicated vs hosted and whether there are cost implications.
[04:33] Diego Ramos: Will do.
[04:35] [04:35] Maya Chen: Moving to holiday capacity — you mentioned earlier an anticipated 3x spike on Black Friday?
[04:40] Rachel Park: We model a 2.8–3.4x spike depending on discounts we run. We need both capacity and a degrade plan so we don't hit 503s.
[04:49] Diego Ramos: We typically recommend a staged degrade: first reduce max completion length, then fall back to a lighter model variant, then queue non-critical requests. With TX-based fallback and cached templates for cart updates you can preserve core flows.
[05:04] Tom Alvarez: What's the latency delta when falling back to the lighter model?
[05:07] Diego Ramos: Lighter 7B variant gives about 30–45% faster latency and 40–55% lower cost per token, depending on sequence len. But quality varies by prompt.
[05:18] Rachel Park: Hmm ok. Simone, will finance sign off on a standby pool + burst?
[05:22] Simone Li: We need the numbers but yes, if it ensures no revenue loss during peaks. Send the scenario pricing.
[05:27] Maya Chen: We'll send two scenarios: conservative (higher standby ratio) and aggressive (lower standby ratio) with modeled cost and revenue protection estimates.
[05:36] Diego Ramos: Also for risk mitigation we can enable automatic fallback to smaller models at the edge with enforced canary thresholds.
[05:45] Rachel Park: Switching topics — procurement and contracts. Our legal wants a data processing addendum and SOC 2 type II evidence.
[05:52] Maya Chen: We have a standard DPA and SOC 2 package — Lena will share the redacted report and the DPA template.
[05:58] Lena Ortiz: Sharing now — I'll drop links after the call and include contact for security review.
[06:03] Tom Alvarez: One technical nit: do you support VPC peering or private link for direct traffic?
[06:09] Diego Ramos: For Dedicated we support VPC peering and private link; for Private deployments we can do on-prem connectors. Hosted supports TLS endpoints but not peering.
[06:19] Benji Reid: And network egress — if we do cross-region burst is there a bottleneck or throttling?
[06:25] Diego Ramos: We provision dedicated egress for committed customers; for burst we have soft quotas. We'll include bandwidth guidance in the benchmark doc.
[06:35] Rachel Park: Let's talk about the pilot acceptance criteria. Our internal suggested criteria: no more than 2% regression in personalization quality metrics, p95 latency under 230ms for the majority of traffic, and a 20% reduction in cost per 1k tokens vs current baseline.
[06:51] Diego Ramos: Those are measurable. We may need to relax the cost goal if strict p95 is required.
[06:58] Maya Chen: We'll capture the acceptance criteria in the pilot SOW.
[07:02] [07:02] Simone Li: Procurement timeline — we aim to approve vendor by 8/12 to align with budget cycle. If pilot starts in early July that gives ops time to validate.
[07:12] Maya Chen: Great. Any other blockers?
[07:15] Tom Alvarez: Just the prompt set and the p95 target; I'll get those to Diego by 6/11.
[07:20] Rachel Park: And I'll confirm sample user cohorts for A/B testing.
[07:24] Maya Chen: Okay recap: Diego to send benchmark plan and kick-off invite; Maya to send pricing scenarios and SLAs; Lena to share SOC2 & DPA; Tom to share prompt set; Simone to confirm procurement timeline.
[07:37] Diego Ramos: I'll also include a suggested degradation flow for Black Friday with model fallback configs.
[07:42] Benji Reid: One last thing — observability retention. We need 90-day raw logs kept for compliance. Is that available in Dedicated?
[07:50] Lena Ortiz: Yes — dedicated customers can opt into raw log retention for up to 12 months with additional storage fees.
[07:56] Simone Li: Ok that's fine.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Cool — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Thanks everyone.
[08:04] Rachel Park: Thanks all.
[08:06] [END]

Notes: transcript has light ASR noise, occasional speaker label issues; timestamps approximate.
